speaker: alse_pinder
text: Water, sir. Mistress said to bring it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Set it on the sill. Keep off the paper.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: There is a blot as big as a groat.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is a blot. I am well.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You are well on the stair, then, and you will be well over broth. Broth is your dinner. You are not going out for it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Titus plays at two. I am not in it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Titus dies at two whether you are there or not. Come down when the cat is off your book.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He is on the Golding. He may stay till I need the page under him.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I do not read the book, sir. I can see the cat.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Master Verbeke ate, and went to his loom. You may do the first of those when the corner is cut.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have a corner to cut, and then the lines. Tell them I am well.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: A twelvemonth and a day, sir. That is what you told the floor on Saturday. Do they marry, or do they not?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: They do not marry. Not today. Keep off the paper, Alse. The half-line is still empty, and it is not your business to fill it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: She has asked. You have answered. Come to the broth before it skins.
